correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the operator argument from the published identities. The Gaussian part has eigenvalues \(c_\beta q^{|\nu|}\), giving its \(r\)-th trace exactly. The correction \(R=B-A\) is positive finite rank with \(\|R\|_1=1-\operatorname{tr}(A)=O(\beta^{-d})\), while \(\|A\|\le\|B\|=O(\beta^{-d})\). Noncommutative telescoping therefore gives an \(O(\beta^{-dr})\) trace-power error. The resulting \(r=2\) case reproduces the published variance asymptotic, and the cumulant and Berry--Esseen deductions use standard independent-sum identities. The finite-sample joint-limit case is explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: The result supplies a structural quantitative refinement of a newly proved Gaussian boundary regime. It identifies the effective spectral power scale at every fixed order, shows that standardized cumulants decay in a complete hierarchy \(\beta^{-d(r-2)/2}\), exposes the dimension-independent leading excess-kurtosis coefficient \(12\), and converts the source qualitative Lyapunov argument into an explicit Kolmogorov-rate order. These quantities are directly relevant to moment and p-value approximations for the BHEP limiting law rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
